counterexample_attempts: The Hall-factor carrier was stress-tested at the legal endpoints d=101 and d=p−1; all degrees, matching conditions, and incidence counts remain valid.

Under the note's averaged θ-reaching definition, the uniform-in-θ reading of Ω(p/ε) fails. The compatibility graph on the p(p+1) lines has minimum degree at least d(d−1), hence a total dominating set of size O(p(p+1)log(p)/d²). For d=(p−1)/2 and θ=1/d this is O(log p)=o(p/ε), while it is θ-reaching.

P11 can be repaired with a single carrier sequence: fix d=101 and let p grow. Then Var(a_x)=ε(1−ε) and Γ₂/ε² tends to 100/101, while every fixed-θ reaching family costs Θθ(p/ε). Thus both proposed incidence-only alternatives fail on the same tables.
The k-direction construction was recomputed for every integer 1≤k≤p+1. Constant zero/one labels give ε=k/(p+1) and Γ₂=k(k−1)/[p(p+1)].
Neither extremal construction is a soundness counterexample: the single polynomial Q=0 agrees with f everywhere.

exponent_audit.reference: KTZ Revision 1, Section 4 and Lemmas 4.1–4.2; numbered note 0056 and 0190–0193

exponent_audit.claim: The KTZ worst-case closure produces ε³=Ω(d/p).
exponent_audit.justification: Uniformly bounding D by O(sqrt(dp/ε)) and imposing D=O(εp) gives dp/ε=O(ε²p²), hence ε³=Ω(d/p). This is a sufficient worst-case gate, not an instancewise necessity; the note correctly warns that KTZ gives only one-sided bounds.
There are p(p+1) lines, each with exactly d accepted points, among p²(p+1) incidences, giving ε=p(p+1)d/[p²(p+1)]=d/p.

exponent_audit.claim: The fractional reaching scale is Θ(p/ε).
exponent_audit.justification: The exact bounds are correct, but uniformly in θ they give Θ(θp/ε). Writing Θ(p/ε) or Ω(p/ε) requires θ to be fixed independently of p and d.

exponent_audit.claim: The collision exponent is exactly quadratic.
exponent_audit.justification: Γ₂=ε²−ε(1−ε)/p+Var(a_x)/[p(p+1)], and constant accepted point degree makes the variance zero. Thus density alone cannot force ω(ε²).

exponent_audit.claim: The Vinh/KTZ component step has a method barrier at exponent 1/2.
exponent_audit.justification: The relevant spectral coefficient is (p+1)^(−1/2). For fixed d=101 and ε=C(101/p)^α with fixed α>1/2, εsqrt(p) tends to zero, so KTZ's absorption inequality eventually fails.
exponent_audit.reference: KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.1, 4.1, and 6.2; numbered note 0197–0209

exponent_audit.claim: The balanced Stevens–de Zeeuw diagnostic gives N≫k^(15/7).
exponent_audit.justification: kN≤I(P,L)≪N^(22/15) gives N≫k^(15/7). Making this bound dominate kp requires k≳p^(7/8), which forces N≳p^(15/8), incompatible asymptotically with N≪p^(15/11).

exponent_audit.claim: The balanced Cartesian diagnostic gives N≫k^(8/3).
exponent_audit.justification: Theorem 4 gives kN≪N^(11/8)+N, hence N≫k^(8/3). Dominating kp requires k≳p^(3/5), forcing N≳p^(8/5), outside N≪p^(4/3).
It does not. Since 0<d/p<1, an exponent α>1/3 would give a smaller and therefore stronger trigger than (d/p)^(1/3). No such unconditional trigger is proved.

line_audit.justification: There are p(p+1) affine lines, p points per line, and p+1 lines through each point. Uniform-line-then-point sampling is exactly uniform sampling from the p²(p+1) incidences.
The formulas are coherent and exclude the target line. Indicator weights recover ordinary selected-line families.

line_audit.claim: The optimum is attained despite being defined as an infimum.
line_audit.justification: Weights above one may be truncated to one without reducing any capped load. The feasible set can therefore be restricted to a nonempty closed subset of the compact cube [0,1]^[p(p+1)], where the objective attains its minimum.

line_audit.justification: At x there are a_x(a_x−1) ordered accepted pairs. Averaging, using E[a_x]=(p+1)ε, and expanding the variance gives the displayed identity. The assumption ε≥2/p is sufficient for Γ₂≥ε²/2.
Each point lies on exactly one line in every direction, so accepting k direction classes makes a_x identically k. The constant labels have degree at most the ambient d.
The selection, interpolation, and root-budget scales are correct. The cubic comparison is explicitly presented as a reconstruction from one-sided source bounds.
The asymptotic calculation for fixed d=101 and fixed α>1/2 is correct and is properly characterized as a method obstruction rather than a theorem counterexample.

The written proof invokes one example against each alternative, which does not by itself refute a universal disjunction. The conclusion is true but requires using the same Theorem-A carrier and computing its variance, together with an explicit asymptotic sequence.
They correctly distinguish architecture obstructions from soundness counterexamples and acknowledge the missing connectivity and algebra-sensitive cases.

All constructed roots are distinct, every formal line degree is below p, vertical lines use fixed affine parameterizations, and no derivative, resultant, factorial, or probabilistic existence is used in Theorem A or Lemma B.

summary: REVISE. The exact SHA was confirmed. The Hall construction, exact degree counts, polynomial realization, fractional sandwich, collision identity, prime-characteristic handling, single decoder Q=0, and all incidence/exponent calculations are correct throughout m=2, prime p, and 101≤d<p. No soundness counterexample or fatal obstruction exists. Strict acceptance fails because the hashed prose conflates pointwise and averaged reaching, suppresses θ in an Ω claim that is false uniformly under the note's definition, leaves k and the collision agreement parameter improperly bound, and P11's written proof negates its two alternatives using different examples. These are repairable. No exponent beyond 1/3 is proved; because d/p<1, any exponent greater than 1/3 would be the genuine improvement.
verified_exponent: No new soundness exponent. The unconditional benchmark remains 1/3; exponents greater than 1/3 would be stronger because 0<d/p<1.
